purpose: 第六章像素角色与教学动作

prompts.motion:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: production pixel art sprite atlas for a character design learning website.
Create one PNG sprite sheet, exactly 6 columns by 4 rows, each cell exactly equal size; overall landscape 1536x1024. Transparent background. NO text, no labels, no grid lines, no scenery, no shadow outside the sprite. Each character fully inside its own cell with ample margins. Every sprite same scale, baseline, palette, face, proportions.
Subject: a very cute friendly tiny explorer, about 3 heads tall, dark short fluffy hair, warm light skin, small teal green jacket, navy shorts/trousers, chunky dark boots, amber small backpack and loose mustard scarf. Clear silhouette, charming expressive body language. Handcrafted 32-bit pixel art game aesthetic, crisp square pixels, limited colors, carefully shaded pixel clusters, no smooth vector curves, no blur, no anti-aliased illustration. Side-facing three-quarter toward right for all action poses, except first row frontal gestures. Character occupies about 60% height of each tile, centered baseline at 85% tile height.
24 cells in exact reading order:
Row 1: 1 neutral front standing with arms down; 2 front wave with right upper arm raised and forearm vertical; 3 same wave forearm tilted outward; 4 same wave forearm tilted inward; 5 quiet encouraging nod with one hand reaching forward; 6 deeper quiet encouraging nod.
Row 2: eight-frame walk is not needed: instead six consecutive frames of one confident walking cycle facing right, alternating planted heel, passing, toe off; backpack and scarf natural. Columns 1 through 6 sequential walk poses with clear bending knees.
Row 3: six jump poses facing right: 1 neutral stand; 2 deep anticipation crouch arms back; 3 takeoff arms raised; 4 airborne apex knees bent; 5 landing deep bent knees; 6 recover standing.
Row 4: 1 stop standing with backpack and scarf hanging normally; 2 same stopped body with scarf and backpack swinging forward; 3 same stopped body with scarf swinging back; 4 happy small celebration arms up; 5 happy leap arms wide with legs bent; 6 happy landing arms out.
Keep all objects contained in their tile. No decorative stars or borders. Precisely aligned regular tile layout is essential.
prompts.study:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: pixel art character study atlas, 4 columns x 2 rows of equal square cells, overall 1536x768. Transparent background, NO labels/text/grid. Each tile a full-body cute 3-heads-tall explorer same scale and baseline 85% down tile, centered and fully contained, ample margin. Crisp handcrafted 32-bit pixel art with clear square pixels and charming careful shading, not vector. Subject same across all eight cells: dark short fluffy hair, warm light skin, teal jacket, navy trousers, chunky dark boots, small amber backpack, loose mustard scarf.
Exact tile reading order:
Top row: 1 clean front standing, simple easily readable silhouette with right arm raised waving; 2 deliberately busy cluttered alternative of that same character: tiny extra badges, many hanging straps, scarf/bag crowding torso and raised arm close to head; 3 clean front neutral with arms down; 4 consistent right-facing three-quarter neutral, identical head-to-body ratio, jacket hem, backpack size.
Bottom row: 1 consistent right side profile neutral with SAME proportions and backpack; 2 deliberately inconsistent right profile variant, head 40% larger, backpack much wider and torso shorter; 3 character holding one large heavy cardboard box to right of torso, convincing grounded wide feet, bent knees, leaned-back torso counterbalancing the box, hands visibly supporting underneath box; 4 identical character and same sized box positioned to right, intentionally unconvincing weight: very narrow feet directly under straight upright torso, rigid straight legs, straight arms reaching forward, combined box/body center of mass outside support base.
This is an educational anatomy/character-design comparison, keep intended readable vs busy, consistent vs drifting, grounded vs unbalanced differences visibly distinct. No text or arrows, no ground plane, no decorative scenery. Each tile independent with no crossing boundaries.
prompts.ball: Transparent cute golden pixel ball, limited palette, crisp square pixels; no text or scenery.
